summary: Senior Cambodian officials, including Deputy Prime Minister Prak Sokhonn, held a briefing for foreign diplomats in Pursat province to address ongoing border tensions with Thailand. The Cambodian side presented maps alleging that Thai forces have illegally occupied areas following military clashes in December 2025. Officials emphasized that any lasting peace must be based on 'truth, accountability, and respect for sovereignty.'
title: Experts call for truth-based border peace

summary: The National Food Institute (NFI) warned that ongoing border tensions with Cambodia could result in a 40-billion-baht loss for Thai food exports in 2026. This adds to existing economic challenges, including the closure of the Strait of Hormuz and a slowing global economy, which are collectively dampening Thailand's export forecasts for the year.
title: Food exports poised to drop by over 7%

summary: The Royal Thai Army reported an incident at the Chong Chom border crossing in Surin province where armed Cambodian soldiers reportedly engaged in provocative behavior toward Thai personnel. In response, Thai forces adjusted their positions and deployed M113 armored personnel carriers to control the area and prevent escalation. Thai authorities emphasized that their actions follow existing joint agreements and aim to maintain safety without escalating the situation.
title: Army Reports Cambodian Soldiers Cause Disturbance at Chong Chom, Provoking Thai Troops

summary: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul announced that the government will include the cancellation of the 2001 memorandum of understanding (MoU 44) on overlapping maritime claims with Cambodia in its upcoming policy statement to parliament. The move comes as the government reviews land boundary deals following recent tensions.
title: Thailand to cancel sea-boundary deal wth Cambodia

summary: The Royal Thai Navy has identified a Thai vessel suspected of illegally transferring 6,000 liters of diesel to Cambodian ships at sea. Additionally, authorities in Trat province seized three Cambodian fishing boats and arrested six crew members for smuggling frozen crab meat into Thailand and preparing to take Thai goods back across the border during this period of high security tension.
title: Navy identifies Thai vessel in sea fuel smuggling; Navy seizes Cambodian boats for goods smuggling

summary: The Thai-Cambodian Situation Information Center reported that Thai forces deployed M113 Armored Personnel Carriers to the border area near Chong Jom, Surin province. The move follows reports of Cambodian soldiers approaching Thai barbed wire fences in a 'provocative' manner. Thai officials clarified that while ASEAN Observation Teams (AOT) from the Cambodian side visited the area, they remained on Cambodian soil. The Thai military maintains its stance of non-provocation but remains ready to protect the border based on the Joint Statement issued in late 2025.
title: เปิดข้อเท็จจริง “ช่องจอม” เขมรป่วนแนวชายแดน ไทยเสริมกำลังทันที ยัน AOT ลงพื้นที่ฝั่งกัมพูชาไม่ล้ำแดน
titleEn: The truth about Chong Jom: Cambodia provokes at the border, Thai forces reinforce immediately, AOT confirmed to stay in Cambodian territory

summary: Prime Minister-elect Anutin Charnvirakul has confirmed that the cancellation of the 2001 MOU regarding overlapping maritime claims with Cambodia will be a core part of the new government's policy statement. Anutin, who is scheduled to lead the Cabinet in taking the oath of office on April 6, 2026, met with military and naval chiefs to solidify this position. The move targets resources in the continental shelf that have been stalled for over 20 years. The military insists that any resource-sharing must be tied to clear maritime boundary demarcation.
title: Thailand to tear up MOU 44 as Hun Sen blocks border reset

summary: Sixteen media and civil society organizations have issued a joint statement demanding the release of two Cambodian journalists sentenced to 14 years in prison. The reporters were convicted after posting photos taken near Prasat Ta Kwai, which showed Cambodian soldiers with landmines in the background. The Appeals Court in Battambang recently upheld the lower court's harsh sentence from December 2025. Rights groups argue the sentence is excessive and stifles reporting on sensitive border issues.
title: Media groups call for release of Cambodian journalists jailed for border photos

summary: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul has publicly condemned the illegal smuggling of fuel across the Thai-Cambodian border, labeling it a direct threat to national security. The statement comes amid heightened economic pressures and an energy crisis, as the government seeks to tighten controls on cross-border trade.
title: PM slams fuel smuggling to Cambodia as security threat

summary: Thai naval authorities in Trat province intercepted three Cambodian fishing boats and arrested six crew members for illegally entering Thai waters to smuggle consumer goods. Two of the boats were specifically crossing to pick up supplies at coordinated spots near Khlong Yai. The crews claimed they resorted to smuggling due to severe economic difficulties.
title: Thai Navy Seizes Three Cambodian Fishing Boats Smuggling Goods, Crews Cite Economic Hardship

summary: The Thai government and military have reiterated their commitment to the General Border Committee (GBC) framework following a visit by the ASEAN Observer Team (AOT) to the Cambodian side of the border. Thai officials emphasized that Cambodia coordinated the visit in advance and confirmed that all activities remained strictly within Cambodian territory without encroaching on Thai sovereignty.
title: Thailand Reaffirms GBC Framework Following ASEAN Observer Team Visit to Cambodian Side

summary: Interior Minister Anutin Charnvirakul has ordered an investigation into an organized network hoarding fuel and diverting supplies for illegal export to Cambodia. Multiple agencies including the police, military, and AMLO are working together to track suspects as the illegal activity is impacting domestic energy security.
title: Fuel-smuggling probe kicks off

summary: The Thai military has deployed armored vehicles to the border following what it described as 'provocations' from the Cambodian side. Officials stated that Thailand is acting with professionalism and restraint to build trust, but the situation remains stable and under control with no active confrontations reported today.
title: Thai Military Deploys Armoured Vehicles to Border After Cambodian 'Provocations'

summary: Air Chief Marshal Prapas Sornjaidee, director of the Thai-Cambodian Information Center (JIC), reported that Cambodian soldiers exhibited provocative and undisciplined behavior near the barbed-wire fence at Chong Chom, Surin province. In response, the Thai military deployed M113 armored personnel carriers to secure the area and prevent escalation. The JIC clarified that the ASEAN Observer Team (AOT) remained within the Cambodian side near a casino and did not enter Thai-controlled territory.
title: Cambodian Soldiers Found Lacking Discipline at Chong Chom, Thai Military Adjusts Forces to Control Area

summary: The Royal Thai Army reported that armed Cambodian soldiers caused disturbances near the Chong Chom border crossing to provoke Thai forces on April 2. Meanwhile, the Burapha Force facilitated a visit for ASEAN Observer Team (AOT) observers in Sa Kaeo province to monitor the situation, which was reported as orderly.
title: ทบ.รายงานเหตุ ทหารกัมพูชาพร้อมอาวุธ ป่วนช่องจอม ยั่วยุทหารไทย

summary: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul confirmed that the Thai government intends to cancel the 2001 Memorandum of Understanding (MoU44) regarding overlapping maritime claims in the Gulf of Thailand. This policy will be formally presented to Parliament. While land boundary agreements (MoU43) remain under review, the move to scrap the maritime deal follows years of stalled negotiations and recent border tensions.
title: ไทยล้มโต๊ะแบ่งขุมทรัพย์ทะเล 'ฮุน เซน'ขวางรื้อเขื่อน-ฉีกMOU43

summary: Air Marshal Prapas Sornjaidee, director of the Joint Information Center (JIC), confirmed that Thai troops were deployed to the Chong Chom area after Cambodian soldiers approached barbed wire lines provocatively. He also clarified that the ASEAN Observer Team (AOT) from the Cambodian side remained within Cambodian territory and did not enter Thai-controlled areas. Thailand maintains its stance of non-provocation and adherence to the December 2025 Joint Statement.
title: Joint Information Center Clarifies Chong Chom Situation, Denies AOT Encroachment

summary: Major General Winthai Suvaree, spokesperson for the Royal Thai Army, reported a tense situation at the Chong Chom border crossing in Surin. Between April 1 and April 2, 2026, Cambodian soldiers reportedly approached Thai barbed wire defenses in a provocative manner. In response, the Suranaree Force deployed M113 armored personnel carriers to secure the area and prevent further escalation, maintaining a strict defensive posture as per the late 2025 Joint Statement.
title: ช่องจอม จ.สุรินทร์ มีความเคลื่อนไหวทหารเขมร พร้อมอาวุธ!!

summary: Local residents in Surin reported seeing mysterious flashing lights, believed to be drones, flying deep into Thai territory (up to 50km from the border) for over 30 minutes. This occurred following reports of aggressive behavior by Cambodian troops at the O Smach-Chong Chom border. Thai authorities have moved M113 armored vehicles to the border gate to deter provocations, while locals express fear that the incidents are 'psychological warfare' intended to trigger a clash during Thai troop rotations.
title: Drones Spotted Over Surin Skies Following Cambodian Provocations, Thai M113s Deployed at Border

summary: Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul convened an urgent meeting with energy and security agencies at Government House. The discussion followed reports of illegal vessels smuggling oil for sale in Cambodia. Navy Chief of Staff Admiral Tadawut Tadpitakkul confirmed that the Navy is monitoring shipping routes and strictly enforcing government policy to ban these exports.
title: นายกฯ เรียกถกด่วน! หลังพบเรือลักลอบขนน้ำมันขายกัมพูชา
titleEn: PM calls urgent meeting after finding vessels smuggling oil to Cambodia

summary: Prime Minister Hun Manet has ordered an investigation into reports of illegal oil being smuggled from Thailand into Cambodia. He asserted that Cambodia has been sufficient in fuel from other sources since June 2025 and does not rely on Thai oil, threatening to revoke licenses of any companies or officials involved in the illegal trade.
title: Hun Manet denies Cambodia needs Thai oil, orders probe

summary: Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet has ordered an urgent investigation into illegal fuel smuggling from Thailand following reports from Thai media and authorities. He warned that any fuel companies involved in the cross-border network would face immediate license revocation and strict legal action. This comes after Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul flagged a suspected smuggling network, describing those involved as 'bad actors' threatening economic security.
title: Hun Manet vows licence revocation for any company tied to fuel smuggling from Thailand

summary: Cambodian authorities and Senate President Hun Sen have called for a peaceful resolution through existing bilateral mechanisms, despite Thai media reports of provocations. Cambodia claims Thai forces have occupied disputed areas with containers and barbed wire. Reports indicate that over 94% of the 640,000 people displaced by previous clashes have returned home, though several schools and health facilities in border provinces like Oddar Meanchey and Banteay Meanchey remain closed.
title: Cambodia pursues peaceful border solution, boosts aid to displaced

summary: Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet has ordered an investigation into claims of illegal fuel smuggling from Thailand, asserting that Cambodia has sufficient domestic fuel stability and does not need to rely on Thai imports. He warned that any fuel companies or military personnel found involved in smuggling would face severe legal action and permanent dismissal.
title: Cambodian PM denies need for Thai fuel imports amid smuggling allegations

summary: Cambodia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs issued a formal protest on April 4, 2026, alleging that Thai forces committed 'unlawful actions' in border regions between March 31 and April 2. The report claims Thai Burapha forces led civilians to verify land ownership near pillars 45-47 in Banteay Meanchey. Additionally, Cambodia alleges that 70 Thai military personnel with armored vehicles installed barbed wire at the O'Smach gate and used heavy machinery to clear land in Anlong Veng. Cambodia views these as unilateral physical changes that violate past de-escalation agreements.
title: Cambodia lodges formal protest against Thai border incursions

summary: Outgoing Defence Minister Gen Nattaphon Narkphanit reflected on the border clashes between July and December 2025 during his farewell ceremony. He revealed that he had privately urged his Cambodian counterpart, Gen Tea Seiha, to withdraw troops before the fighting broke out, but those efforts failed. He defended his silence during the conflict, stating that sensitive military plans could not be disclosed to the public or the neighboring country.
title: Outgoing minister reflects on clashes

summary: The Royal Thai Army has increased border defenses in Surin after reporting 'provocative actions' by Cambodian soldiers between Wednesday night and Thursday morning. Army spokesman Maj Gen Winthai Suvaree stated that armed Cambodian personnel approached the Thai line in an undisciplined manner, violating the December 27 joint statement. In response, Thai troops installed additional barbed wire and deployed two M113 armored personnel carriers to deter further escalation.
title: Surin border tensions flare

summary: Thai security forces from the Burapha Task Force and Aranyaprathet Rangers, in coordination with Cambodian counterparts, repatriated 49 Cambodian nationals (27 men, 19 women, and 3 children) at the Ban Khlong Luek border checkpoint in Sa Kaeo. The group was pushed back after their legal cases in Thailand were completed. Both sides coordinated closely at the Thai-Cambodia Friendship Bridge, reflecting positive relations between local border agencies despite broader tensions.
title: Return home! Aranyaprathet-Cambodian officials push 49 workers out of Thailand after legal cases conclude

summary: Defense Minister Lt. Gen. Adul Boonthamcharoen stated that Thai authorities, including the Marine Department and the Thai Maritime Enforcement Command Center (Thai-MECC), are strictly monitoring fuel smuggling into Cambodia. He noted that ships in the Gulf of Thailand are being tracked via GPS, and any vessels turning off their signals will be considered suspicious. The statement follows Prime Minister Anutin's condemnation of fuel smuggling as a national security threat.
title: Defense Minister addresses fuel smuggling at Thai-Cambodian border

summary: Thai Defense Minister Lt. Gen. Adun Boonthamcharoen stated that the situation at the Thailand-Cambodia border remains normal with no signs of immediate clashes. He cautioned the public against believing social media rumors, describing the current disinformation atmosphere as a 'Hybrid War' intended to cause division.
title: “บิ๊กดุลย์” มั่นใจคุมกลาโหม ไม่หวั่นชายแดนไทย-กัมพูชา เตือนอย่าเชื่อข่าวลือยุคสงครามไฮบริด
titleEn: Defense Minister confident in border control, warns against 'Hybrid War' rumors

summary: On April 4, 2026, Thai authorities at the Ban Klong Luek Permanent Border Checkpoint in Aranyaprathet deported 49 Cambodian nationals (27 men, 19 women, and 3 children) after their legal cases in Thailand were finalized. Cambodian coordination officials received the group at the border bridge, and the process was described as orderly and cooperative.
title: 49 Cambodians Deported from Thailand via Poipet After Legal Cases Conclude

summary: The Cambodian government has filed a formal protest against the Thai military, alleging 'unlawful and repeated activities' in disputed border zones near Preah Vihear Temple and O'Smach. Reports claim Thai troops conducted land-clearing and deployed armored vehicles on April 2, 2026. Cambodia also reported that schools and health centers in border provinces remain closed due to the ongoing tension.
title: Cambodia protests Thai activities in disputed border areas

summary: The Royal Thai Navy is closely monitoring the arrival of a Chinese-made Type 056 (Jiangdao-class) missile corvette at Cambodia's Ream Naval Base. The vessel arrived on April 4, with an official handover ceremony scheduled for April 8. A second corvette is expected in June 2024. Thai officials are concerned about the rapid expansion of Cambodian maritime power and the presence of advanced weaponry, including anti-ship and air-defense missiles, near the Gulf of Thailand.
title: Thai Navy monitoring Cambodia's receipt of Chinese missile-guided corvette on April 8

summary: The new Thai government under Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul is set to deliver its policy statement to Parliament on April 9-10, 2026. A key foreign policy and security objective involves addressing the Thailand-Cambodia maritime and land border issues through peaceful means and existing bilateral mechanisms. Crucially, the government plans to study the cancellation of the 2001 Memorandum of Understanding (MOU 44) regarding the Overlapping Claims Area (OCA) in the Gulf of Thailand, amid concerns that the agreement risks Thai sovereignty over Koh Kood.
title: Government reveals 'Anutin 2' policy statement, seeking to cancel MOU 44

summary: Economic analysts and the Thai Chamber of Commerce have assessed that the ongoing border instability between Thailand and Cambodia over the past six months has resulted in trade losses exceeding 80 billion baht. Border trade and investments have slowed significantly due to the security situation. The Thai-Cambodian Business Council has urged the new government to find ways to resolve the conflicts to restore economic confidence, especially at key trading hubs like Rong Kluea Market which has seen a sharp decline in activity.
title: Commerce Chambers Estimate 80 Billion Baht Loss from Border Instability

summary: Defense Minister Lieutenant General Adul Boonthamcharoen dismissed rumors of a third round of border clashes with Cambodia, urging the public to trust official military reports. He noted that if fighting were to break out, the military would issue warnings and evacuate civilians immediately. He also addressed a petition regarding the influencer 'Gun Jompalang,' explaining that private assistance like fuel and bunkers was helpful during past crises when government budgets were slow, but all border activities must now be strictly regulated. Additionally, he highlighted efforts to monitor oil tankers in the Gulf of Thailand to prevent illegal price manipulation.
title: Defense Minister confident third round of fighting has not occurred; orders tight control over oil tankers

summary: The Royal Thai Army organized a media visit to the border area in Surin province to showcase an alleged scam center operating in O Smach, Cambodia. Military officials stated that current troop deployments follow existing agreements. While the Army is ready for self-defense if provoked, they emphasized that there is no immediate cause for concern regarding border security at this time.
title: Thailand takes media to 'O Smach scam centre' on Thai-Cambodian border in Surin

summary: Air Chief Marshal Prapas Sornchaidee led an inspection of the O Smach-Chong Chom border area in Surin, which is currently under Thai military control following late 2025 border skirmishes. The massive 'scam city' complex, once hosting 10,000 workers, contained 160 buildings divided into seven zones. Investigators found torture chambers, a private hospital, and scripts for 'pig butchering' scams targeting victims in the US, Europe, and Asia. The Thai military states the area was seized because it was used as a base for launching attacks during the conflict.
title: O Smach ‘Scam City’ contained torture cells, a private hospital and a global fraud network

summary: Air Marshal Prapas Sornjaidee, Director of the Thai-Cambodian Situation Information Center, led domestic and international media to the Chong Chom border area in Surin province. The visit aimed to inspect the 'O Smach Scam Center,' a large transnational crime network. The Thai military clarified they are not blaming Cambodia but pointing at a shared international problem. They emphasized that Thai troops are strictly following border agreements and international law without any territorial encroachment.
title: Military takes media to O Smach scam center to prove border situation remains under control

summary: Lieutenant General Adul Boonthamcharoen reassured the public and investors that the Thai military is fully prepared to defend national sovereignty following two previous clashes. He stated that there are currently no warning signs of renewed conflict and encouraged tourists to visit Kantharalak district and natural sites like Pha Mor E Daeng during the Songkran holiday. He emphasized that the situation is under control and residents can continue their lives normally.
title: Minister plays down border fears, encourages tourism in Si Sa Ket

summary: Political activist Sonthiya Sawatdee submitted a letter to the Minister of Defense calling for an end to military support for influencer Guntouch Pongpaiboonwet (Gun Jompalang) at the border. Sonthiya raised concerns about potential conflicts of interest regarding the influencer's foundation and private sales. He specifically pointed out incidents where civilians engaged in arguments with Cambodian soldiers, which he claims could damage the image and discipline of the Thai military and provoke unnecessary tension between the two nations.
title: Sonthiya petitions Defense Minister to stop 'Gun Jompalang' activities at Thai-Cambodia border

summary: Defence Minister Lt Gen Adul Boonthamcharoen stated that while any new clash would be a major confrontation, the chances of renewed fighting are very low. He urged residents at the border to celebrate the Songkran festival normally, as contingency plans are in place. He noted that the 'opposing side' would have to consider their readiness before fighting Thailand again. The Minister also mentioned a planned visit to boost troop morale during the holidays.
title: Cambodia would weigh any third clash with Thailand carefully, says defence minister

summary: On April 7, 2026, the Joint Information Center (JIC) on the Thailand-Cambodia Situation led 28 journalists from 15 foreign media outlets to Surin Province. This site visit aimed to allow international media to observe the areas affected by recent border clashes and receive briefings from Thai Ministry of Foreign Affairs officials on the current security situation.
title: Foreign journalists visit Surin to observe Thai-Cambodian border conflict areas

summary: Journalists were given a tour of the O'Smach Resort complex, a massive 197-acre site that the Thai military seized in December 2025. The military claims the site was used by Cambodian forces as a base for attacks and as an industrial-scale scam center. The complex, linked to sanctioned Cambodian politician Ly Yong Phat, reportedly housed up to 10,000 workers involved in global online scams. Construction is still visible on the site, highlighting the industrial scale of the operations that Thailand is attempting to shut down.
title: Inside a Huge Compound on Thailand-Cambodia Border Where 10,000 Workers Scammed People Globally

summary: Defense Minister Lt. Gen. Adul Boonthamcharoen urged social media influencers to act ethically and avoid creating content that heightens border tensions for views. He addressed concerns over recent clashes, stating that military intelligence shows no immediate signs of a 'third round' of fighting, but warned that inaccurate information from influencers causes unnecessary stress for frontline troops. He also defended the transfer of Captain Thammanoon Wanna, an officer with combat experience in the area, to a mine-clearing unit as a logical move based on his expertise.
title: Defense Minister advises influencers on Thai-Cambodian border content: Do not pressure soldiers

summary: The Thai Prime Minister issued a statement regarding the ongoing border situation, asserting that Thailand is not the aggressor and has not initiated any conflict. However, the government maintained a firm stance that it will not tolerate any violations of Thai sovereignty. The administration called for public confidence in the military and noted that all operations are conducted based on reason, security, and humanitarian principles.
title: Prime Minister addresses Thailand-Cambodia border situation, insists Thailand did not initiate and will not allow sovereignty violation

summary: Army Chief Gen. Pana Klaewplodtook has ordered the construction of 182 bunkers along the Thai-Cambodian border to ensure civilian and troop safety following a de-escalation of regional fighting. The project, divided between the Burapha Task Force (108 bunkers) and Suranaree Task Force (74 bunkers), is reportedly 80% complete with 117 units finished since December 2025. The military aims to restore local confidence and allow residents to resume normal lives.
title: ประชาชนต้องปลอดภัย! ผบ.ทบ. สั่งเร่งสร้าง 182 หลุมหลบภัย เสริมมั่นคง "ชายแดนไทย-กัมพูชา"

summary: Cambodia has issued a formal warning to Thailand, stating that any attempt to withdraw from the 2001 Memorandum of Understanding (MoU 44) regarding maritime boundaries and joint resource sharing would damage years of bilateral cooperation and trust. This comes amid ongoing domestic political pressure in Thailand to review the agreement.
title: Cambodia Warns Thailand Against Scrapping 2001 Maritime MOU

summary: The Royal Thai Navy's spokesperson, Rear Admiral Parat Rattanachaiphan, strongly denied allegations of military involvement in border bribes or supporting illegal activities along the Thai-Cambodian border in Chanthaburi. The Navy highlighted its recent success in arresting individuals attempting to enter Thailand illegally and seizing smuggled goods worth over 16 million baht, in addition to significant quantities of drugs including over 18 kilograms of crystal meth.
title: Royal Thai Navy denies border bribe allegations, confirms 872 arrests for illegal entry

summary: At a ceremony on April 8, Malaysia received drones and rescue boats from Japan to assist the ASEAN observer team monitoring the Thai-Cambodian border. Malaysia, the former ASEAN chair, facilitated the truce following 2025 fighting that killed 30 people. The leading role of the observer team will be handed over to the Philippines by the end of April. Currently, Thai rangers continue patrols near Aranyaprathet to monitor for illegal activity.
title: Malaysia receives Japan equipment for team observing Thai-Cambodia conflict

summary: Thai military officials conducted a media tour of a border crossing in Surin province on Tuesday to refute allegations regarding the presence of scam centers and to address security concerns. This follows reports of massive scam compounds, such as the O'Smach Resort in Cambodia, which Thailand previously targeted during border clashes to prevent their use as operational bases for attacks.
title: Thai Military Escorts Media to Border to Counter Scam Center Allegations

summary: Phnom Penh has officially requested a Joint Boundary Commission (JBC) meeting to resume land demarcation, while protesting what it calls 'unlawful' activities by Thai armed forces in disputed areas. The Cambodian government proposed a six-point plan, including dispatching joint survey teams between April 20-24 to Banteay Meanchey and Battambang provinces. Spokesman Pen Bona urged Thailand to cease unilateral actions and reduce tensions, alleging that Thai troops have occupied territory in four border provinces following military friction last year.
title: Cambodia calls for urgent JBC talks with Thailand over illegal border occupation

summary: The Royal Thai Army is accelerating the construction of 182 safety shelters along the Thai-Cambodian border to protect soldiers and civilians. Army Chief Gen Phana Klaewplodthuk reported that construction is 80% complete, with 117 sites finished. The project is divided between the Burapha Task Force (108 sites) and the Suranaree Task Force (74 sites) to ensure residents can return to normal life following the easing of recent border clashes.
title: Thai Army speeds up building 182 shelters to boost safety on Thai-Cambodia border

summary: The Thai military has officially dismissed claims from Phnom Penh that Thai forces encroached on Cambodian territory near the Chong Chom border crossing. Thailand maintains that its troops are stationed within agreed-upon boundaries to tackle transnational crimes emanating from 'scam compounds.' The military reaffirmed its adherence to the December 2025 Joint Statement, which mandates maintaining current troop positions to avoid escalation.
title: Thai Army Rejects Cambodia Incursion Claim at Chong Chom Scam Site

summary: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul announced plans to build a border wall and is accelerating a study to potentially terminate the 2001 Memorandum of Understanding (MOU 2001) regarding overlapping maritime claims with Cambodia. He emphasized prioritizing national interests and sovereignty while addressing transnational issues such as scam networks and narcotics.
title: Anutin pledges border wall, speeds up MOU2001 termination study

summary: The Joint Information Center on the Thailand-Cambodia Situation released a statement clarifying that Thai troop positions at the Chong Chom border area in Surin are defensive and comply with the December 2025 GBC agreement. The statement reveals that the area under Thai control was previously used as a military base and an industrial-scale scam compound by forces from the Cambodian side. Evidence found includes large quantities of foreign SIM cards and multilingual scam scripts, proving the site was a hub for transnational cybercrime.
title: Regarding Allegations of the Presence of Thai Troops in the Chong Chom Border Area

summary: The Joint Information Center on the Thailand-Cambodia Situation (JIC) clarified on April 10 that the presence of Thai soldiers near the Chong Chom border in Surin province is a defensive measure to prevent military threats and crack down on transnational crimes, specifically 'scam centers.' The military insists these actions are limited in scope and do not infringe on Cambodian sovereignty, despite allegations from the Cambodian side.
title: Army Rebuts Cambodia: Thai Control of 'Scam Centers' at Chong Chom is Not Incursion

summary: Army chief Gen Phana Klaewplodthuk announced that the Royal Thai Army is accelerating the construction of 182 civilian shelters along the Thai-Cambodian border. While recent tensions have eased, the military is prioritizing resident safety, with 117 shelters already completed under the Burapha and Suranaree Task Forces. The project is over 80% complete and aims to allow local communities to return to normal daily life despite ongoing frontier sensitivity.
title: Security, shelters boosted along Cambodia border

summary: Thai authorities have responded to Cambodian accusations regarding the Chong Chom border area, insisting that Thailand is strictly following General Border Committee (GBC) agreements. Officials stated that recent military movements are security measures aimed at tackling transnational scam centers that used the area as a base. Thailand emphasized cooperation over confrontation to solve border crimes and maintain regional stability.
title: Thailand insists on GBC agreement, denies encroaching on border territory

summary: Thai media reports that while there has been no direct armed clash today, Cambodian troops are engaging in 'daily provocations.' This includes moving forces close to the Thai border and allegedly burning forest areas before blaming Thai soldiers for the fires. The report frames these actions as attempts to disturb the peace along the border despite Thailand's commitment to existing border agreements.
title: Cambodian Movements: Daily Provocations Against Thailand

summary: The Thailand-Cambodia Joint Information Center (JIC) issued a formal rebuttal to Cambodian allegations regarding Thai troop movements at the Chong Chom border in Surin province. Thailand insists it is strictly following the GBC agreement from December 2025 to maintain troops in current positions. The military explained that the presence of soldiers is a 'defensive' and 'preventive' measure against transnational crime, alleging that Cambodian forces have used the area as a base for military attacks and large-scale 'scam compounds.' Thai officials emphasized transparency and invited the media to inspect the site.
title: Thailand Rebuts Cambodia's Claims on Chong Chom Border! Confirms GBC Agreement Upheld, No Incursion

summary: Cambodia has issued a warning to the new Thai government regarding signals that Thailand might cancel MOU 44, which governs overlapping maritime claims. Cambodia claims that a unilateral withdrawal would violate international law and damage energy cooperation in the Gulf of Thailand. The statement emphasizes that the agreement should remain in effect until its objectives are fully met through mutual friendship.
title: กัมพูชาเตือนไทย! ปมยกเลิก MOU 44 ชี้ละเมิดกม.ระหว่างประเทศ
titleEn: Cambodia warns Thailand over MOU 44 cancellation, citing international law violations

summary: The Thai-Cambodian Situation Information Center (JIC) has officially denied allegations from Cambodia regarding Thai military presence in the Chong Jom area. Thai authorities provided photographic evidence asserting that their operations strictly follow the General Border Committee (GBC) agreements. Thailand countered that the area in question has been used by transnational scammer networks and as a military base, necessitating security measures that do not violate sovereign agreements.
title: Thailand Rejects Cambodian Claims, Confirms Compliance with GBC Agreements at Chong Jom Border

summary: Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow described the current border atmosphere as fragile, stating Cambodia must choose between peace or loss. The new Thai government, led by PM Anutin Charnvirakul, is preparing to propose the cancellation of MoU 44 (the 2001 maritime overlapping claims agreement) to the Cabinet. Additionally, there are plans to reduce visa-free stays for Cambodians from 60 to 30 days to bolster national security.
title: Sihasak Warns Border Situation Fragile; New Government Moves to Scrapping MoU 44

summary: Deputy PM Anutin Charnvirakul is criticized for moving slowly on the controversial 2001 MOU regarding overlapping maritime claims with Cambodia, choosing to 'study' it rather than cancel it as some nationalists demand. title: PM reveals border fence budget for Thai-Cambodia-Malaysia sent to military; Scraps MOU 44 citing it's 'useless'

summary: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul clarified that the decision to revoke the 2001 Memorandum of Understanding (MOU44) with Cambodia is based on the lack of progress over 26 years rather than current border tensions. He confirmed that budgets for border fences along the Thai-Cambodian and Thai-Malaysian borders have already been allocated to the military. Thailand plans to shift to the UNCLOS framework for future maritime negotiations.
title: PM Anutin states MOU44 cancellation due to 26 years of zero progress, not conflict

summary: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul confirmed that the government has allocated budgets for building border fences along the Cambodian and Malaysian borders. He stated that the first phase is already underway in border provinces and the project must be continuous to ensure national security. Regarding the reopening of Thai-Cambodian border crossings, the PM stated it is not yet the time to discuss that matter.
title: Prime Minister Anutin reveals border fence construction for Cambodia and Malaysia borders with allocated budget

summary: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul announced that the budget for constructing a border fence along the Thai-Cambodian border has been allocated to the military. The first phase is underway in border provinces, with additional funding requested for remaining sections. Anutin also confirmed the decision to cancel the 2001 MOU on maritime claims, stating it has been stagnant for 26 years and no longer serves national interests. He urged patience regarding Cambodian 'provocations' in their own territory, stressing that Thai forces will stay firm as long as the border line is not crossed.
title: PM reveals border fence budget reached military; insists on canceling MOU44 due to lack of benefit

summary: Prime Minister Srettha Thavisin stated that Thailand is moving forward with constructing border fences to enhance national security along the borders with Malaysia and Cambodia. Regarding the reopening of Thai-Cambodian border checkpoints, the PM mentioned it is not yet the time to discuss that matter, focusing instead on security infrastructure.
title: PM reveals Thailand proceeding with border fences to boost security with Malaysia and Cambodia

summary: Following the 2025 border escalation, China has hosted 'Track II' dialogues in Beijing to foster peace. The April 20-21 session involved think tanks and media from all three nations to implement the 'Fuxian Consensus'. The dialogue emphasizes an 'Asian Security Model' focused on shared interests and humanitarian cooperation independent of sovereignty disputes.
title: China Mediates Thai-Cambodia Rift with Dialogue

summary: Defence Minister Lt Gen Adul Boonthumjaroen announced that Thai-Cambodian border checkpoints will remain closed indefinitely. He stated that reopening is contingent on Cambodia's compliance with the existing ceasefire agreement and bilateral mechanisms. This follows the Thai government's formal cancellation of the Memorandum of Understanding 44 (MoU44) on Thursday.
title: Cambodian border to remain shut

summary: The Thai government maintains a strict closure of border crossings, citing Cambodia's failure to adhere to the December ceasefire agreement (Joint Statement). Defence Minister Adul emphasized that existing frameworks like the Regional Border Committee (RBC) and General Border Committee (GBC) remain the primary channels for communication, but no personal-level negotiations have begun.
title: Thai-Cambodia border stays shut amid ceasefire non-compliance

summary: Reports on April 25, 2026, indicate increased military activity at the Thai-Cambodian border near 'Chong Cham Tae'. Cambodian soldiers have moved their positions closer to the Thai line and hung blue mesh-like cloths (similar to sunshade nets) in clearly visible spots, possibly to mark coordinates or boundaries. Thai military officials have urged an end to provocative behaviors to avoid potential clashes, describing the current atmosphere as tense despite no active fighting yet.
title: Cambodian Soldiers Move Bases Close to 'Chong Cham Tae' Border, mysterious Blue Cloths Raised

summary: The Cambodian government has issued a warning following Thailand's National Security Council (NSC) resolution on April 23, 2026, to unilaterally cancel the 2001 Memorandum of Understanding (MOU44). Cambodia expressed regret, stating the move undermines the mutual intent to explore underwater resources in the Overlapping Claims Area (OCA) of the Gulf of Thailand. Cambodia reaffirmed its commitment to the MOU and noted that recent legal steps by Cambodia regarding maritime boundaries under UNCLOS should facilitate, not hinder, cooperation.
title: Cambodia Warns Thailand Over Unilateral Cancellation of MOU44, Impacts Joint Development Plans

summary: Residents in Ban Kruat District, Buriram Province, are calling on the Thai government to fulfill a campaign promise to build a border wall between Thailand and Cambodia. The villagers expressed anxiety over previous clashes and current territorial disputes. They voiced support for the cancellation of MOU43 and MOU44, claiming Cambodia has failed to adhere to past agreements, and believe a wall is necessary to prevent further sovereignty incursions.
title: Villagers in Ban Kruat demand border wall construction, fearing repeated disputes

summary: Thai media reports indicate tension in Sa Kaeo province after satellite imagery suggested Cambodia has been diverting natural waterways since 2015-2018, potentially affecting border lines. Thai Rangers are monitoring the Khlong Nam Sai area. Additionally, viral clips show Cambodian soldiers surveying war debris at Preah Vihear Temple and conducting military training sessions, which some Thai netizens interpret as preparations for potential renewed conflict.
title: Observing Cambodia's movements: Waterway diversion and activities at Preah Vihear

summary: Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow clarified that the Thai government will prioritize land border demarcation with Cambodia following the decision to scrap MoU 44. He emphasized that the termination of the 2001 maritime agreement was a sovereign decision to move past 25 years of stalled talks. Thailand will formally notify Cambodia and seeks to establish a new framework that separates border clarity from resource management.
title: Land Border 'Priority' Over Maritime Claims, Foreign Minister Says

summary: The Thai Army Chief has ordered intensive monitoring of the Thai-Cambodian border. Spokesperson Col. Winthai Suvaree stated that Thailand strictly follows the December 27, 2025, joint statement to maintain current troop positions and avoid provocation. Despite sporadic incidents, coordination remains functional. The RBC meeting on April 23 confirmed cooperation on humanitarian aid and forest fire prevention.
title: Thai Army Monitoring Border Intensively, Insists on Strict Adherence to Joint Statements

summary: Army spokesperson Col. Winthai Suvaree stated today that the Thai military remains on high alert along the Cambodian border despite comments from Chinese FM Wang Yi suggesting Cambodia 'no longer wants to fight.' The army is maintaining its current troop positions and patrolling regularly to ensure security, while adhering to a non-provocation policy. Military intelligence has not yet confirmed any significant shift in Cambodia's tactical stance.
title: Army Spokesperson: Close Watch on Thai-Cambodia Border Continues, Monitoring China's Remarks

summary: The Thai government is moving to cancel the 2001 MOU on overlapping maritime areas, citing 20 years of stagnant progress. Foreign Minister Sihasak clarified that the move does not mean stopping negotiations, but rather shifting the framework to the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) to ensure international standards and fairness. Both sides confirmed their commitment to maintaining the current ceasefire and using existing bilateral mechanisms to manage border tensions.
title: Sihasak officially informs Cambodian FM: Thailand preparing to cancel MOU 44, switching to UNCLOS

source: Daily News (เดลินิวส์)
summary: Army Chief Gen. Pana Klaewplodthook has instructed units to maintain a high state of vigilance and gather intelligence following recent 'scattered' incidents that may have appeared provocative but lacked clear intent. The army spokesperson stated that while both sides are prepared, they remain within their respective sovereign territories. Regarding reports that China offered to mediate, the Thai military emphasizes that they rely on military intelligence over media rhetoric and note that while Cambodia has moved some bases back toward the border post-clash, they have not yet intruded into Thai-controlled areas.
title: Army Chief monitors border closely, says Cambodia's military moves not yet worrying

summary: The Royal Thai Army is closely monitoring the border following comments from Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi suggesting Cambodia no longer wishes to engage in conflict. Army Chief Gen. Phana Klaewplodtuk has ordered troops to remain vigilant, improve defensive positions, and verify intelligence. The army also noted that compensation of 10 million baht for soldiers injured or killed in the first round of clashes has been paid, while the second round is still in process.
title: Army says Wang Yi's words on Cambodia not wanting to fight requires military intelligence verification

summary: Thai Deputy PM and Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow met with Cambodian Foreign Minister Prak Sokhonn in Brunei on April 27. Thailand officially informed Cambodia of its process to cancel the 2001 MOU regarding overlapping continental shelf claims (MOU 44). Sihasak emphasized that Cambodia must stop making 'distorted' public statements if they wish to continue bilateral talks and urged for a better atmosphere to be created before formal border committee (JBC) meetings can resume.
title: Sihasak meets Prak Sokhonn, insists Cambodia stop distorted statements if they want to talk to Thailand

summary: Officials from Cambodia and Thailand met on Monday to discuss border tensions and the potential revocation of MoU 44 regarding maritime claims. While Cambodia expressed concern over unilateral actions and military barriers (shipping containers) placed by Thai forces in Pursat, Thailand maintains these measures are for security. The meeting aimed to manage the ceasefire following last year's armed clashes.
title: Cambodia and Thailand meet for 'candid' discussion on border dispute

summary: A military demining unit (TMAC-1) discovered 32 active anti-personnel landmines in Sa Kaeo province on April 25. The find included 22 PMN and 10 MN79 mines. Since November 2025, over 189 explosive items have been cleared from the area, which was previously a conflict zone. Authorities warn residents to stay away from uncleared zones as the mission continues.
title: 32 mines found in one day near border

summary: Thailand has officially informed Cambodia of its intent to terminate the 2001 Memorandum of Understanding (MoU 44) regarding overlapping maritime claims. Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow delivered the news during a meeting in Brunei, stating that the 20-year-old agreement has seen little progress. Thailand seeks a new framework to better protect its interests, though it insists the move does not mean an end to bilateral talks.
title: Thai-Cambodian maritime pact set for cancellation; Brunei meeting informs Cambodia of decision

summary: The Royal Thai Army reported a tense encounter at the Chong Chom border in Surin Province. While Cambodian officials were escorting a diplomatic delegation to inspect the area, Thai authorities claim Cambodian soldiers repeatedly approached the Thai barbed wire line, violating joint agreements. In response, Thai troops fired three warning firecrackers to signal them to withdraw. Major General Winthai Suwaree stated that Thailand is issuing a formal protest letter, accusing Cambodia of trying to create a false image of Thai aggression.
title: Three Warning Firecrackers Fired as Cambodian Soldiers Provoke Thai Side Near Chong Chom Border Wire

summary: The Thai Ministry of Defence clarified that Thai forces did not use actual weapons during a recent encounter at the Chong Chom border area. Officials stated that soldiers only lit 3 firecrackers to warn Cambodian troops who were moving too close to the Thai barbed-wire fence. This response follows Cambodian allegations that Thai forces opened fire during a visit by foreign military attachés.
title: Ministry of Defence denies using weapons against Cambodia, says only 3 firecrackers were lit as warning

source: The Star (covering Thai Second Army Region)
summary: The Second Army Region of Thailand clarified an incident near the Chong Chom (O'Smach) border crossing on April 29, 2026. After Cambodia alleged that Thai soldiers fired shots near a 'scammer building' close to the border, Thailand officially denied using weapons. The Thai military stated that the loud noises heard were from firecrackers, not bullets, during a period when Cambodian officials were escorting military attachés near the safety boundary line defined by Thai barbed wire.
title: Firecrackers, not bullets — Thailand denies Cambodia accusation

summary: The Thai Army has issued a warning that it will strictly follow military guidelines if Cambodian troops violate border agreements or the December 2025 ceasefire. Tensions remain high due to reported troop movements near the fence and a dispute over dredging at Khlong Nam Sai in Sa Kaeo. Major General Benjapol of the Burapha Task Force insisted the area is Thai territory and that Thai forces will continue to patrol to protect sovereignty.
title: Thai Army vows response if Cambodia breaches ceasefire deal

summary: Thai authorities including the Burapha Force and immigration police prepared to receive 635 Thai nationals at the Ban Khlong Luek border checkpoint in Aranyaprathet. However, Cambodian officials at Poipet have repeatedly delayed opening the border gate without explanation. The group consists of 190 illegal border crossers, 6 people involved in online crime cases, and 2 with arrest warrants. Thai officials are currently attempting to negotiate for their safe return.
title: Tension at Sa Kaeo border: Cambodia refuses to open gate for 635 Thais as agreed

summary: Cambodian authorities have begun the repatriation of the first batch of 350 Thai nationals through the Aranyaprathet border checkpoint. Thai officials are conducting screenings and legal checks, noting that a total of 635 individuals are expected to return under the bilateral cooperation framework.
title: กัมพูชาเปิดด่านส่ง 350 คนไทยชุดแรกกลับประเทศ
titleEn: Cambodia Opens Border, Releases First Batch of 350 Thais Returning Home
